subject.title: fix(plugins): surface oversized-file warnings in doctor migration reads

question: May `openclaw doctor` intentionally skip migration of an existing legacy plugin-state file above 10 MiB, and if so what user recovery contract must accompany that skip?
rationale: The cap is a sensible availability boundary, but it newly changes the treatment of persisted legacy state; code review cannot choose whether avoiding the read outweighs migration continuity for affected existing users.

options.title: Accept bounded migration with explicit recovery
options.body: Keep the 10 MiB cap, preserve the source file, and require a clear warning and documented user remediation path.

options.title: Preserve migration continuity
options.body: Revise the migration design so previously readable oversized legacy state receives a bounded, supported migration path rather than being skipped.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded migration with explicit recovery
recommendation.body: Keep the 10 MiB cap, preserve the source file, and require a clear warning and documented user remediation path.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current migration design and can incorporate the chosen contract, though current-main ownership history was unavailable.
